title: Vernacular Press Act 1878
definition: A draconian legislative measure enacted by Lord Lytton to curtail the freedom of the Indian-language press by empowering the government to confiscate printing presses and demand security deposits for 'seditious' content.
importanceInUpsc: It is a pivotal topic in Modern Indian History, illustrating the colonial state's repressive policy towards nationalist discourse and the subsequent rise of organized political agitation in India.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Vernacular Press Act 1878.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Evolution of Press Laws in India
